strengths: The paper addresses an important question: why adversarial training can preserve clean generalization while producing a large robust generalization gap.

Combining local robust memorization with signal-versus-noise learning dynamics provides an interpretable candidate mechanism. The proposed three-stage account offers useful intuition beyond a capacity argument alone.

The empirical investigation includes MNIST and CIFAR10 capacity sweeps, synthetic feature trajectories, and input-gradient measurements. These complementary measurements are relevant to the stated objectives.
weaknesses: Theorem 4.4 is false under the stated assumptions. Consider a balanced distribution on two well-separated atoms with a small, clean-accurate but adversarially vulnerable classifier; this satisfies Assumptions 4.1–4.3. As the sample size grows, both atoms appear with substantial empirical frequency, so vanishing robust training error forces vanishing robust population error, precluding CGRO. Additional assumptions controlling population coverage are necessary. Moreover, Assumption 4.2 separates opposite classes, whereas Lemma 4.5 incorrectly infers that all training balls are disjoint.

The ReLU approximation argument in Theorem 4.4 and Appendix F has another substantive gap. Continuous ReLU networks cannot uniformly approximate a generally discontinuous indicator-based function f_S to arbitrarily small error. Replacing indicators with continuous transitions does not establish the claimed uniform approximation. Furthermore, small function-value error alone does not preserve classification without margin control. The construction needs an explicit treatment of transition regions and their effect on all three classification errors.

Theorem 5.9 does not establish robustness under the paper's original definition. Definition 5.6 restricts attacks to the true-signal direction in the meaningful patch, leaving noise patches unchanged. Definition 3.3 instead maximizes over the full perturbation ball. Appendix E.12 infers small robust training error from the restricted adversarial loss, which does not control full-ball robust training error. This distinction is central because the proposed mechanism relies on memorizing the protected noise patches.

The clean-generalization proof also contains invalid probabilistic arguments. Appendix E.12 treats sums of cubed Gaussian projections as sub-Gaussian, although cubic Gaussian variables have heavier tails and projections across filters share the same test noise. Its inference that every noise-weight norm is Θ(1) from aggregate training memorization is also unjustified. Additionally, Assumption 5.7 allows c_alpha > 1/2, for which typical positive initial signal components already exceed the induction bound O-tilde(alpha^-1) in Hypothesis E.1. These issues require substantive corrections to the dynamics analysis.

The synthetic experiment does not validate the theorem's stated regime: Section 6.2 sets delta = alpha = 10, despite the required strict inequality delta < alpha. The permitted attack can therefore erase the entire label-bearing signal, making robust population error at least one half unavoidable even for an optimal classifier. The image experiments demonstrate generalization gaps but do not isolate the proposed memorization mechanism from optimization effects. Missing PGD step counts, step sizes, restarts, and repeated-run uncertainty further limit assessment and reproduction.

The claimed novelty of the representation lower bound is insufficiently established relative to Li et al. (2022). Theorem 4.7 is existential, and Appendix F still constructs linearly separable data; the manuscript should identify precisely what stronger guarantee its broader clean-classifier assumption yields. The worst-case exponential lower bound also does not establish that capacity causes the observed gaps on the structured distribution or image benchmarks.

The additional generalization bound in Theorem B.1 is unsupported as stated. A constant nonzero classifier has zero input gradient, yet its label-dependent logistic loss can have population risk exceeding empirical risk with nonvanishing probability, contradicting the claimed high-probability bound with no additional sampling term. Appendix G also leaves density-estimation bias and variance terms that disappear from the final statement without justification. This undermines the supplementary explanation based on global flatness.
